Adopter migrations can leave PRE-EXISTING unmarked duplicates untouched by design (no marker to collapse); a post-migration grep for the section heading OUTSIDE the marker block is a cheap completeness check worth adding to the migration ledger routine.

Regression tests through the public API alone could not reach the legacy fallback path (new slices always get id_suffix stamped); the honest test had to seed a legacy unstamped slice directly. When fixing fallback-path bugs, test the fallback's precondition explicitly.

Uniqueness gate scoped to new writes only: done/FEAT-005 carries a pre-existing duplicate id_suffix that no automated path re-parses, but a MANUAL slice from-feature --id FEAT-005 would now hard-fail — deliberate and attributable, recorded here as the ledger caveat.

Testing an unref'd-by-design timer needs a ref'd keepalive across the await: with no other ref'd work, Bun's event loop idles before the unref'd timer fires and the whole suite hangs at collection. The production unref stays — the test must supply the liveness.

A builder's pre-apply STOP on a dry-run diff (kb's 130-line body vanishing) caught a latent inter-span deletion bug that 18 prior green migrations never exercised — marker spans happened to be adjacent everywhere else. Estate diversity, not test count, exposed it.

Installer appends new marker blocks at file END while legacy blocks sit at file TOP — any multi-span collapse tool must treat the gap between them as protected content, never as span-adjacent whitespace.
Content-debt backfill against a validator is only trustworthy when the validator itself stays byte-identical — the review's first check must be 'diff the validator', not 'run the validator'.

The universals-drift check silently degrades to skip when the plugin cache namespace is stale ('loop' post-rename) — marker presence is enforced but hash freshness is dormant; render-universal-skills.mts PLUGIN_NAMESPACES needs a follow-up fix.

CAVEAT (required, do not mark satisfied): AC-8b remains OPEN — the commits.find() first-match selection in git-anchored-completion.mts still carries the FEAT-294 gap; tracked upstream, flagged in-code at the call site. This close covers AC-1/2/4 only.

The hand-rolled frontmatter parser silently nulls object-map keys starting with '-' — any id_suffix-keyed structure must be an array of mappings, not an object map. Verified live: object-map parses to null, no error.

mixed-shape proposed_slices_shipped fails open to [] by design — reachable only via hand-corrupted frontmatter (sole writer emits homogeneous arrays) and self-heals on next write since the field is a non-gating audit trail.

The migrateShippedFrontmatter neuter is caught by unit tests only; integration fixtures re-derive fresh git evidence per run and never exercise carry-through. Unit-level coverage is the load-bearing net here.

The audit's 'same store' framing for learn/lessons-recent was wrong — code trace showed learnings.jsonl vs grade files; executing a consolidation plan still requires re-verifying each pair's premise in code.

Shared-index race: a pathless `git commit` in the main session swept another builder's staged files under the wrong message (content intact, history commingled). All lead commits are now pathspec-scoped (`git commit -- <paths>`); wave-mode worktree isolation remains the structural fix.

Contract said 4 sanctioned cross-imports; ground truth was 10 across 3 files (crew-bridge, phase-gate). Boundary contracts drafted from partial grep evidence must be re-derived by the implementer with real path resolution before enforcement lands.

Static-import regex missed the repo's dominant lazy-loading idiom (dynamic import()) — a reviewer's live bypass probe caught it; widened same-session. Enforcement scanners must cover the codebase's actual import idioms, not just the textbook one.
The preset gate went born-red on a preset the FEAT never named (dotnet-python) — glob-all-and-guard beats enumerate-the-known-offenders for referential-integrity gates.

Keeping a known-dead rule (stack:vue -> vue-engineering) in the production matcher table ON PURPOSE turns silent drift into a loud unresolved report — reproducing the origin defect as a live rule is a legitimate guard pattern.

A dispatch-level chokepoint guard is only as complete as the list of dispatchers: three rawArgv short-circuits (dispatch/config/wave) bypassed the main COMMANDS registry, and two of them still carried the bug after the 'complete' fix. Enumerate every dispatch surface before claiming a chokepoint covers the CLI.

The reviewer's read-only-analog probe (wave plan --help proving run/loop's shared structure) is how you safely verify destructive paths — prove the mechanism on the harmless sibling, fix structurally, then live-test once the guard is the first statement.
The builder re-triggered the exact bug being fixed mid-task against the real repo — P0 arg-safety defects stay dangerous during their own repair; work in temp fixtures from the first command.

Release order matters for self-referential gates: registry pushed first, sync gate verified locally against the LIVE registry, only then the version-bump commit + tag — the reverse order red-flags every consumer's CI for the gap window.

The decisive ADR evidence was mechanical, not judgmental: TS7's package.json exports map simply does not export the classic compiler-API surface, so openapi-typescript's ts.factory import cannot resolve — verified against installed packages, not docs. When a design decision has a physically-checkable premise, check it before weighing preferences.
The dynamic-glob referential gate (preset-skill-ids) made this deprecation a zero-test-change operation — guards that derive their fixture set from the filesystem absorb estate changes for free.

Reference sweeps need a live-vs-historical discrimination rule: scrubbing point-in-time evidence docs destroys the audit trail that JUSTIFIES the change. Live docs updated; dated analysis/retro content preserved.

Runtime-split validators (bun lib + dependency-free node parity copy) are a real drift surface — the review proved parity by piping identical edge receipts through BOTH processes, which is the only honest check; a shared fixture corpus should ride any future schema change.

Templates with load-bearing structured output (pm's file-based results, swarm's return block) must get new contracts APPENDED, never substituted — tracing the actual consumer (pm-apply reads --file, not message text) beat assuming the doc's own description.

Remediation text is part of the enforcement surface: a guard whose block message recommends a token the same guard blocks is a dead end no string-contains assertion catches. The systemic fix — a test that parses the successor map and live-asserts every recommended token passes — guards the class, not the instance.

Root `bun run typecheck` covers two tsconfigs, not crew/tsconfig.json; a lane that only runs the root script can leave CI gate 36 red. Lane gate lists must name all three projects.

Fixing the aggregation without fixing the dispatch prompt would have reintroduced last-writer-wins under a different key — the stock reviewer wrote no --reviewer at all. Check who produces the key, not just who consumes it.

A deliberately-red test needs its red state documented where a CI reader looks, not only in the FEAT body: the verifier found gate 41 red with nothing in docs/ci-gates.md or docs/memory.md explaining it. A designed-red gate without a paper trail reads as a broken branch.

Test helpers that stage a full repo copy must own their teardown from the first commit: two stagings per run at ~269 MB on a persistent self-hosted runner, with the test red indefinitely, is an unbounded disk leak that no assertion catches.

A guard is only as real as the call path it sits on. FEAT-025's refusal logic landed in maybeEmitCostReport (interactive /crew:build) while this repo's own closes go through costSliceHandler via crew-bridge; both reviewer B and the verifier caught it independently from the same live evidence — zero of 57 cost reports carried run_id. Grep the callers before declaring a cross-cutting contract done.

Silent pricing fallbacks hide model drift for months: every fable-5-1 session was billed at sonnet-4 rates until priceFor stopped prefix-matching. Exact-key-or-date-suffix matching plus an explicit unpriced_models list makes the gap visible instead of plausible.

Root `bun run typecheck` covers tsconfig.json + tsconfig.test.json, not crew/tsconfig.json, and tsconfig.test.json runs strict:false where an awaited discriminated union does not narrow from a bare truthiness check under TS 7. Use `=== true` and say why, or the error reappears as a mystery in a different project.

A policy that must read identically in five prompt files is only stable when a test asserts the exact sentence and the forbidden phrases; prose review alone let the five docs contradict each other for months. command-gate-policy.test.mts now pins the sentence and the three banned phrasings.

Any new root -> crew/ import (here validation-gate.mts -> crew/scripts/lib/ci/consumer-ci.mjs) must be registered in validate-repo-boundary.mts ALLOWED_CROSS_IMPORTS in the same commit or gate 9 goes red; follow the existing phase-gate.mts entry rather than widening the rule.

A wave open that rotates currentRun once per lane leaves every lane worktree carrying the LAST slice's run title; reviewer/validator gates still record correctly because the close gate reads status, not title, but cost attribution and run-brief paths point at the wrong slice. Open each lane's run inside its own worktree, or rotate after worktree creation.

Replacing a contract in four near-identical prompts needs a test that reads all four; the guardrail-phrase test only read fullstack-dev.md, so two builders kept the old "commit -> PR report" paragraph until a reviewer read them by hand. builder-report-contract.test.mts now asserts the legacy phrases are absent in every builder.

Decision ids are allocated per branch at close time, not reserved by the spec: a spec that says "DEC-040" is a placeholder. Lanes that mint a DEC file directly must renumber at merge; let grade-write allocate instead, or check the branch's highest id right before committing.

A validator rule keyed on frontmatter `tools:` is inert for every agent that omits the field. Treat absence as all-tools unless `disallowedTools` names the capability, and keep a fixture that fails for the absent-field case.
